Manuscript validation contract (package 0.1.0)

Source: VALID_STRATEGY.md

validate_manuscript(path, output_format = NULL, check_environment = FALSE) and render preflight use validate_manuscript_context(). Rendering enables environment checks. validate_render_environment() retains its environment-only API.

Inputs and metadata

Explicit .qmd paths resolve independently of the caller’s working directory. Directory/NULL input selects exactly one immediate .qmd; missing and ambiguous inputs retain DIAG-INPUT-001/002/003. The nearest _quarto.yml/.yaml establishes the project boundary. Extensions are discovered between manuscript and that root.

Project, ancestor directory _metadata.yml/.yaml, then front matter are merged. Mappings merge recursively; sequences merge; document format names select outputs while matching format options inherit. Resource paths in each YAML source resolve relative to that source directory (project settings relative to project root). Resource validation does not use the caller’s working directory.

Required and optional fields

All three variants require a non-empty text title and format: typstR-typst (or the equivalent mapping). typstR.format-variant defaults to workingpaper and also accepts article or brief. Article/brief are variants of the same bundled format, not separate Quarto format names.

Authors, affiliations, abstract, keywords, JEL codes, report number, statements and branding remain optional for every variant, including anonymized articles. Omit optional fields when unused. Supplied subtitle/abstract and inline include text must be text, not sequences, mappings or null. Quarto rejects null for typed standard fields such as abstract and bibliography; change inherited settings with a valid value or edit their declaring configuration. When present, author names, IDs, emails, ORCIDs, booleans, lists, colors and margin lengths are checked for supported shapes. Affiliation IDs must be unique; references to a declared ID table must resolve.

Configured bibliography, CSL, logo and header/body include files must exist and be files. Citations in prose and narrative metadata need a bibliography or inline references; fenced/inline code examples are ignored. Inline references must be a sequence of mappings with unique text IDs. Remaining bibliography contents and citation-key resolution are delegated to Quarto/citeproc; successful creation alone does not prove meaningful PDF content. Required render assurance checks PDF text, warnings and representative layout separately.

Diagnostics and limitations

Existing codes retain their assignments. DIAG-MANUSCRIPT-001 covers YAML syntax or mapping errors; 002 format/variant; 003 metadata shape; 004 missing resources; 005 unsupported configuration. Diagnostics retain severity/location/hint and are sorted using the shared deterministic ordering contract.

This preflight supports static local YAML. Profiles (including QUARTO_PROFILE), .local project overrides, metadata-files, executable !expr YAML and remote resources are rejected explicitly. Generated resources must exist before calling the helper. It does not parse code-generated citations, arbitrary filters, shortcodes, publisher styles, font availability or the full Quarto schema. Inline include {text: ...} is supported. Use Quarto directly with manual verification for unsupported configurations. Do not interpret a static pass as visual approval.

Reference semantics: Quarto project metadata.
